MODULE: apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/pause-context.tsx (52 lines). FOUR exports:

A component rendered with no provider above it (a unit test, a stray mount) reads null and must render nothing rather than crash or say "not paused".
- `pauseWords(paused: ProviderPause): string` - USE THIS, do not re-format. It returns exactly `Agents paused: <provider> limit, resumes <when>`, where `when` is `new Date(Date.parse(resetAt)).toLocaleString()` and falls back to the RAW `resetAt` string when `Date.parse` is NaN (3a's decoder only gates resetAt on non-emptiness, so unparseable instants really do arrive; printing "Invalid Date" or dropping the pause are both forbidden). Same idiom as `agentsWords` at ops-screens.tsx:59. If your surface needs different wording (e.g. a Seats row that omits "Agents"), extend pause-context.tsx with a second exported formatter rather than inlining a template literal - one file owns the pause vocabulary.

WHERE THE VALUE COMES FROM: cordum-app.tsx wraps `<CordumShell>` in `<ProviderPauseProvider value={paused}>` (:394), so EVERY screen rendered as shell children can call the hook - Seats, board, goals, all of them, with no extra wiring on your side. TESTING NOTE that will save you an hour: `vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true })` advances the fake clock by REAL elapsed time, so any handshake await silently eats into the interval you are measuring and a "one tick short" negative fires early. Use PLAIN `vi.useFakeTimers()` and settle the handshake by flushing microtasks at zero fake time (`await act(async () => { await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0); })` in a bounded loop until your element exists).
